item.title: There Are Exactly $2^\mathfrak{c}$ Simultaneously Bireflective and Bicoreflective Subconstructs of $\mathbf{FTS}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that there are exactly $2^\mathfrak{c}$ simultaneously bireflective and bicoreflective subconstructs of $\mathbf{FTS}$. By the Lowen--Wuyts bijection, these correspond to the total fuzzy topologies contained in $M$, the fuzzy topology consisting of all nondecreasing left-continuous self-maps of the unit interval. The upper bound follows from a cardinality estimate. The matching lower bound is obtained by encoding $2^{\mathfrak c}$ ultrafilters on $\mathbb N$ into total fuzzy topologies contained in $M$.
item.dc:creator: Gao Zhang

item.title: Soft normed linear spaces via soft elements: decomposition, convergence, and operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.35879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F\colon A\to\mathcal{P}(X)$ be a soft linear subspace of a linear space $X$ over $\mathbb{K}$. Its soft elements form the product $\prod_{t\in A}F(t)$. We use this representation to characterize selection spaces, decompose soft norms and soft linear operators into their sectionwise parts, and compare soft, uniform, and componentwise convergence. We also characterize completeness and continuity in the box, extended-supremum, and product settings. Neumann-series and fixed-point results are obtained as applications.
item.dc:creator: Subhasis Ray

item.title: A Radon-Nikod\'{y}m theorem for Fuzzy Number Multimeasures in Locally Convex Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a Radon-Nikodym theorem for dominated fuzzy number multimeasures defined on $\Sigma$ and taking values in $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$, where $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ is a complete finite measure space and $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$ is the family of generalized fuzzy numbers on a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space $X$, i.e., a map $u: X \to [0,1]$ is a member of $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$, if and only if for each $\alpha \in (0,1]$ the $\alpha$-cut $[u]^{\alpha}$ of $u$ is a member of the family $cwk(X)$ of all nonempty convex and weakly compact subsets of $X$, ($[u]^{\alpha} = \{x \in X: u(x) \geq \alpha \}$).
item.dc:creator: Sokol Kaliaj

item.title: Bornologies and Kuratowski-Painlev\'e Convergence to the Empty Set Revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.35907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(X,\tau)$ be a noncompact metrizable space and let $\langle T_n\rangle$ be a sequence of nonempty closed sets converging to the empty set in the sense of Kuratowski--Painlev\'e. The subsets of $X$ whose closures meet at most finitely many terms form a bornology $\mathcal B_\tau(\langle T_n\rangle)$. We give an internal criterion for inclusion between two such bornologies and recover each of them from a canonical free filter of closed sets. In fact, a nontrivial bornology is sequence-induced exactly when it has the enlargement property and its closed polar has countable character. Our principal result says that the bornology of relatively compact sets is sequence-induced precisely when $X$ is locally compact and separable; in the locally compact case the character of its closed polar is the density of $X$. In the penultimate section, we make a clever use of the sequence $T_n=\{n\}$ in the real line to give a negative answer to a conjecture posed in 2001 about a coarsest topology making the associated bornology a nontrivial metric bornology. Finally, we end the paper with a more general result: a coarsest such supertopology exists if and only if the original topology already makes the induced bornology a nontrivial metric bornology, in which case the coarsest supertopology is the original topology itself.
item.dc:creator: Basile Beyer de Ryke, Gerald Beer

item.title: Closed Lindel\"of $\Sigma$ Kernels of Neighborhood Assignments in Charming Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every neighborhood assignment on a charming space $X$ has a countable kernel whose closure in $X$ is Lindel\"of $\Sigma$. Consequently, for any two neighborhood assignments $M$ and $N$ on $X$, there is a closed discrete set $D\subseteq X$ such that $M[N[D]]=X$. We give an exact one-step formulation of the remaining $D$-space problem and identify the universal pointwise square-refinement condition with the classical $z$-space condition. For continuous closed surjections, we prove a fixed-assignment lifting equivalence. We also show that every uncountable $\mathrm{HFC}_{\mathrm w}$ subspace of $[\omega_1]^{\leq\omega}$ is dually closed countable but not charming. For a fixed Lindel\"of $\Sigma$ kernel $Y$, we iterate the Hu--Yin boundary reduction by a transfinite closed-core process. At every stage, the current iterate is a $D$-space if and only if $X$ is a $D$-space. The iteration stabilizes before $hL(Y)^+$ at the largest closed subspace in which the kernel trace and its complement are both dense. The bound is sharp: for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$ and every $\gamma<\kappa^+$, there is a compact example with a dense $\sigma$-compact Lindel\"of $\Sigma$ kernel $Y$ satisfying $hL(Y)=|Y|=\kappa$ whose first stabilization stage is $\gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: University Research and Leadership in the Age of AI: Mobilizing Intellectual Capacity and Building the Infrastructure for Discovery
item.description: arXiv:2610.35919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) raise the prospect of substantial changes in how research is conducted and who can direct discovery. This perspective argues that universities should prepare for these changes by developing AI as well as using it, rather than relying primarily on capabilities designed elsewhere. The relationship is reciprocal: AI can advance disciplinary research, while scientific questions, experimental evidence, and observed failures can guide AI development. The proposal distinguishes three complementary commitments: shared operation of existing AI models, disciplinary AI development, and foundational AI research. Their resource requirements differ, and no single university needs to reproduce a frontier AI company. Shared computational services should be connected to sustained technical teams, laboratory experimentation, and knowledge records that make findings traceable and reusable. Independent evaluation, alignment research, transparent resource allocation, and inclusive academic governance are integral to this infrastructure. Consortia and national facilities can support capabilities beyond individual campuses while preserving room for investigator-led inquiry. Initial programs in experimental and mathematical research would test scientific value, the effort required to validate results, and improvements to AI before expansion. The argument concerns research rather than educational reform and calls for building institutional capacity before the extent and timing of disruption are settled.
item.dc:creator: Bacim Alali

item.title: On Baireness of the Wijsman Topology
item.description: arXiv:2610.35921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give negative answers to Questions 4.4 and 4.5 in Cao's survey on the Wijsman topology. We construct a metrizable space $Y$ and a compatible metric $d$ such that every finite power $Y^n$ is Baire, while $(\mathrm{CL}(Y),\tau_W(d))$ is not Baire. The construction realizes the Vietoris hyperspace of a suitable metric space as an open subspace of a ball hyperspace. We also study the set $S_d$ of points having an open $\sigma$-$d$-totally bounded neighborhood. We prove that Baireness of $(\mathrm{CL}(X),\tau_W(d))$ implies Baireness of $S_d$, and that, whenever $S_d$ is dense in $X$, the following three conditions are equivalent: $(\mathrm{CL}(X),\tau_W(d))$ is Baire, $X$ is Baire, and $S_d$ is Baire. As consequences, we obtain complete characterizations for locally $\sigma$-$d$-totally bounded metric spaces, countable metric spaces, and $\sigma$-compact metrizable spaces. In our counterexample, $S_e$ coincides with a non-dense discrete component for every compatible metric $e$, showing that the density assumption is essential.
item.dc:creator: Basile Beyer de Ryke

item.title: The Hardy-Littlewood conjectures on the twin primes and the binary Goldbach problem are true
item.description: arXiv:2006.04547v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A celebrated conjecture of Hardy and Littlewood provides with an asymptotic formula for the counting function of the twin primes. We give an unconditional proof of such a formula by means of a finite Ramanujan expansion of the counting function expressed in terms of the von Mangoldt function and its incomplete form. In a completely analogous way, we solve the conjugate conjecture on the representations of any even integer as the sum of two prime numbers.
item.dc:creator: Maurizio Laporta

item.title: Equating the Area Sums of Alternate Sectors of a Disc Cut by Concurrent Chords
item.description: arXiv:2110.12559v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A disc is cut by $n$ chords through a common interior point $O$, which produces $2n$ curvilinear sectors. We determine when the two sums of alternate sectors have equal area for arbitrary chord directions, which need not be equally spaced. We first derive a closed form for the area of a single sector. We then show that the answer depends on the parity of $n$. For even $n$, at fixed orientation the condition is affine in $r_0^2$, where $r_0$ is the distance from $O$ to the centre; it involves only the total angle of the odd sectors and one trigonometric moment of the directions. For odd $n$, the condition is a nonlinear alternating sum of circular-segment functions of the distances of the chords from the centre. We treat four, six and eight pieces in detail. We also hold the chord directions fixed and translate the whole pencil to an arbitrary interior point, and we characterise the direction sets that give equal sums at every such point. For four chords only equally spaced directions have this property, which gives a converse of the pizza theorem; for an odd number of chords no direction set has it. A fair two-chord cut requires the acute angle between the chords to lie within $(r_0/a)^2$ radians of a right angle, where $a$ is the radius. For equally spaced chords the results reduce to the known theorems of Goldberg and of Mabry and Deiermann.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Iqbal, Derek Abbott

item.title: Mixed Hodge Modules and Canonical Perverse Extensions for Multi-Node Conifold Degenerations
item.description: arXiv:2604.05367v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study one-parameter conifold degenerations whose central fiber \(X_0\) has finitely many ordinary double points and construct a mixed-Hodge-module refinement of the corrected perverse variation-cone object associated with the degeneration. At each node \(p_k\), the local \(\can^H/\Var^H/N\) geometry determines a rank-one point-supported interface block \(W_k^H\simeq i_{k*}\Q^H_{\{p_k\}}(-1)\). These blocks assemble canonically into \(Q_\Sigma^H=\bigoplus_{k=1}^r W_k^H\), through which the node-supported monodromy factors. We prove that the perverse-normalized cone \(\Cone(\Var^H)\) is concentrated in the mixed-Hodge-module heart, thereby defining \(\mathcal P^H\in MHM(X_0)\), and that \(\rat(\mathcal P^H)\simeq\mathcal P\). In the forward Yoneda orientation, the point-supported quotient is instead \(R_\Sigma^H\simeq\bigoplus_{k=1}^r i_{k*}\Q^H_{\{p_k\}}(-2)\), exhibiting a Hodge-theoretic distinction invisible after rational realization. We further prove a canonical nodewise decomposition of the rational perverse extension space and construct a morphism from the formal local Hodge sector to the independently defined limiting mixed Hodge structure. Its image records the node contributions that survive in global limiting cohomology, allowing nontrivial global relations among vanishing cycles.
item.dc:creator: Abdul Rahman

item.title: Null Cartan Normal Helices in Minkowski Space-Time
item.description: arXiv:2607.01262v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A complete theory of null Cartan normal helices in Minkowski space-time $\mathbb{E}^4_1$ is developed. Two algebraic conditions, obtained by successive differentiation of the helix invariant along a unit $C$-constant normal field, fully characterize null Cartan helices; the quadratic condition yields two mutually orthogonal helix axes in the Lorentzian metric. Special field types are analyzed and null Cartan cubics are shown to be normal helices. On a timelike hypersurface, a Darboux frame with six curvature functions is constructed from first principles, the normal isophotic condition is shown to reduce to a linear first-order ODE, and the existence of normal silhouettes in $\mathbb{E}^4_1$ is established.
item.dc:creator: Derya Sa\u{g}lam, Umut Selvi
